title: Open Source AI Without the FOMO
subtitle: From evaluation to deployment, in plain English
intro: New AI models drop every week. Your save calls it a "fast-paced mess" — and an open ebook promises clarity from evaluation to deployment.
takeaway: Open source AI lets you test, share, and ship models faster, but only if you evaluate honestly and track licenses.

sections.heading: Analogy: a community kitchen
sections.body:
Think of open source AI like a community kitchen. Recipes (models) are posted for anyone to copy, taste, and improve.

You can borrow a recipe, test it in your kitchen, and serve it to guests. That sharing is why it moves so fast.

But a good kitchen still needs taste-tests and labels, which is where the next idea comes in.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Clarity from evaluation to deployment
sections.body:
Open source AI exists to let anyone build on shared work.

- Model evaluation means taste-testing: does this model actually work for your task?
- AI deployment means serving it safely to real users.
- Licensing like CC-BY-4.0 and Apache-2.0 tells you what you can reuse and how to credit.

The ebook The State of Open Source AI (2023) maps this whole path so you don't chase every new release.

Even with a map, sharing creates risks, as you'll see next.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When sharing breaks
sections.body:
Sharing without checks goes wrong fast.

- A model scores well in a demo but fails on your data because evaluation was skipped.
- You deploy without tracking licenses and get stuck legally.
- Everyone forks the latest model, so nothing stays maintained.

The fix is simple: evaluate before you trust, check the license before you ship.

steps.narration: Start with a shared open model from the community.
Evaluate if it works on your task, not just the demo.
Check CC-BY-4.0 or Apache-2.0 rules for reuse.
Deploy only after tests and license pass.

quiz.q: What does model evaluation do in open source AI?
options: It taste-tests if a model works for your task
quiz.why: Evaluation is the taste-test before you serve — the ebook puts it before deployment.

quiz.q: What fails first if you skip evaluation and deploy the trending model?
options: It may fail on your real data and users
quiz.why: Demo scores don't guarantee your use case — skipping evaluation is the top failure mode.

quiz.q: What does an open license like Apache-2.0 tell you?
options: What you can reuse and how to credit
quiz.why: Licenses govern reuse and credit, not performance.
